a3967.speech: Stressed the importance of integrating the fund's systems with those of service providers as part of digitalization efforts: "ZHSF has initiated this process by integrating our identification and authorization system with the Zanzibar Residence Identity Cards (ZanIDs), allowing our members to access health services using their ZanIDs. We plan to extend this integration to other platforms, such as the National Identification Authority (NIDA)"; emphasized the use of mobile applications to engage the community, raise awareness about available services, and facilitate member enrolment and information updates.

a3967.speaker: Ali Idrissa Abeid, Zanzibar Health Services Fund (ZHSF)
a3967.name: Ali Idrissa Abeid
a3967.title: Zanzibar Health Services Fund (ZHSF)
a3967.speech: Proposed using Artificial Intelligence to process claims from service providers, thereby reducing payment times and controlling fraud: "Currently, service providers may submit claims and receive payments after two to three months due to the mismatch between available human resources and workload. By integrating AI into our systems, we can automate this process, significantly reducing the time it takes to pay service providers."

a3996.speaker: Titi Ogufere, Founder of Design Week Lagos
a3996.name: Titi Ogufere
a3996.title: Founder of Design Week Lagos
a3996.speech: Spoke about the inspiration behind this year's theme: “We feel like it's essential for people to understand, especially in Nigeria, the power of design and what design does in developing any society. If you look at what's happening, we're actually ripe in Africa. Most people can't afford normal furniture, so we have to look inwards, begin to develop what we have, from education to our products to our raw materials” ; emphasised the significance of design in shaping industries and futures, stating that “pretty much everything we see in the world was designed. From the clothes, television, the phone, the floor, everything was designed. And it was designed by people” ; noted that Africa has been focused on importing goods and ideas that may not be suited to the local context, resulting in a lack of originality and innovation: “We're almost all down to copying. I think, for me, more than anything else, it's just the amount of activations and the possibilities that we have” ; highlighted the importance of providing a platform for designers to showcase their work and learn from each other: “We brought in big designers to meet with young designers, to share their experiences and knowledge. We want to create a community that is supportive and innovative” ; “For me, it's not just an experiment. It's one that we believe will help to develop the industry. It will help to make people see that there are other possibilities and other means of income” ; stated that “we're right in the centre, I would say, of developing what we have inwards.”

a3996.speaker: Titi Ogufere, Founder of Design Week Lagos (on the Incubator programme)
a3996.name: Titi Ogufere
a3996.title: Founder of Design Week Lagos (on the Incubator programme)
a3996.speech: Explained that the programme was designed to help designers develop their skills and create products that are affordable and relevant to the local market: “We took them through an Incubator program, we made them try to understand our local raw materials. And we said to them, your product must not be more than 250,000 Naira.”

a3996.speaker: T.Y. Bello, photographer and featured designer
a3996.name: T.Y. Bello
a3996.title: photographer and featured designer
a3996.speech: When asked about her inspiration, said: “I've always been intrigued by light and I felt like I needed to tell a story. The unknown, the spontaneous, the random, and like what I would call the wind of God and how those things sometimes bring fear and uncertainty but they are the things that actually make our lives beautiful.”

a3996.speaker: T.Y. Bello, photographer and featured designer (on the event's theme)
a3996.name: T.Y. Bello
a3996.title: photographer and featured designer (on the event's theme)
a3996.speech: “I think that the most important thing for me is the inclusivity and understanding that everything has changed, every single thing has changed, nothing remains the same and same goes with design. I love the fact that Titi Ogufere, she's a disruptor and she's constantly pushing on those boundaries.”

a4154.speaker: Virginia Palmer, United States Ambassador to Ghana
a4154.name: Virginia Palmer
a4154.title: United States Ambassador to Ghana
a4154.speech: Underscored the importance of maintaining a respectful and balanced partnership between Ghana and the United States, stressing that despite differences in economic scale and historical timelines, the two nations must continue working together as equals: “I think we are equals. Your economy is smaller than mine, and you have been independent for less time than the U.S., but I think we must work together as equals. That is number one.”

a4154.speaker: Virginia Palmer, United States Ambassador to Ghana
a4154.name: Virginia Palmer
a4154.title: United States Ambassador to Ghana
a4154.speech: Clarified changes regarding the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), noting that its functions would now be overseen by the U.S. State Department, a transition consistent with her long-standing view that U.S. development assistance, funded by taxpayers, should serve as a foreign policy instrument and be administered accordingly: “The functions of USAID will now be run by the State Department, by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and that is something, to be honest, I have advocated for decades. I don’t think that will cause any difference in focus or in effect.” ; Reassured that the U.S. remains firmly committed to its development partnership with Ghana and emphasised that the change in administrative oversight will not impact the effectiveness or direction of American assistance ; Reaffirmed Ghana’s continued significance in U.S. foreign policy.

a4160.speaker: Borno residents (spoke with PREMIUM TIMES)
a4160.name: Borno residents (spoke with PREMIUM TIMES)
a4160.speech: Said the shadows cast by the terrorists in the communities remain despite the intensity and successes of the military operation ; said they still could not access their farming and fishing areas.

a4160.speaker: Zagazola Makama, a security expert
a4160.name: Zagazola Makama
a4160.title: a security expert
a4160.speech: Reported that 15 insurgents were killed as soldiers repelled a midnight attack on New Marte.

a4160.speaker: Reuben Kovangiya, an army captain and spokesperson of Operation Hadin Kai
a4160.name: Reuben Kovangiya
a4160.title: an army captain and spokesperson of Operation Hadin Kai
a4160.speech: Said 60 insurgents were killed when they attacked Bita in Gwoza LGA ; said the insurgents had their eyes on the swamped buggies purchased by the Borno State Government for waterways clearance in the Lake Chad region.

a4160.speaker: Local sources
a4160.name: Local sources
a4160.speech: Said the air operation targeting terrorists preparing for Sallah attacks at Chiraliya village resulted in the deaths of over 500 militants, including two prominent Ka’ids (commanders), Abu Dauda and Ya Mohammed.

a4160.speaker: Nigerian Army
a4160.name: Nigerian Army
a4160.speech: Said some soldiers were wounded in the operation.

a4160.speaker: Abdulkarim Lawan, Speaker of the Borno State House of Assembly
a4160.name: Abdulkarim Lawan
a4160.title: Speaker of the Borno State House of Assembly
a4160.speech: Said: “Let me reiterate my appeal for the military to take over the entire Guzamala Local Government Area, which has remained under Boko Haram territory, so as to restore civil authority” ; described a recent bomb explosion in the town as pathetic, but commended security agencies for the successes recorded so far.

a4160.speaker: An elderly man in Baga (anonymous resident)
a4160.name: An elderly man in Baga (anonymous resident)
a4160.speech: “We heard that the top commanders of Boko Haram who killed our farmers were also killed, and we are happy,” commending soldiers for the development.

a4160.speaker: A resident of Kukawa (anonymous)
a4160.name: A resident of Kukawa (anonymous)
a4160.speech: “We hear gunshots almost every night. But when we see Boko Haram around and we tell soldiers in the town, they would not go.”

a4160.speaker: A resident (anonymous)
a4160.name: A resident (anonymous)
a4160.speech: Complained that food was also a problem as NGOs’ support had reduced drastically and the government had been reluctant to support them with food: “Boko Haram are saying we must register with them before we can farm, and they are killing us. Support from NGOs is also not coming.”

a4160.speaker: Abubakar Hassan, a resident of New Marte
a4160.name: Abubakar Hassan
a4160.title: a resident of New Marte
a4160.speech: “We used to have a Brigade Command but it was moved to Dikwa. Patrolling of the area is poor. But recently, I noticed they brought more soldiers” ; “They (insurgents’) spare women but for men, no matter how small you are, they will just kill you.”

a4160.speaker: A resident of Gwoza (anonymous)
a4160.name: A resident of Gwoza (anonymous)
a4160.speech: “We are with our soldiers. We are going to fight Boko Haram alongside our troops. This time around, we are not leaving them to destroy our town.”

a4160.speaker: A source in Wulgo who fled to Gamboru Ngala (anonymous)
a4160.name: A source in Wulgo who fled to Gamboru Ngala (anonymous)
a4160.speech: “As I am speaking to you, there is no single soldier in Wulgo.”

a4160.speaker: Babagana Zulum, Governor of Borno State
a4160.name: Babagana Zulum
a4160.title: Governor of Borno State
a4160.speech: Celebrated the recent successes of the troops; mourned the fallen soldiers and volunteers, offering N5 million to each family and a scholarship for their children.

a4160.speaker: Sahara Reporters (report)
a4160.name: Sahara Reporters (report)
a4160.speech: Reported that over 300,000 insurgents reportedly repented and were de-radicalised in the last three years and were subsequently handed over to the Borno State Government.

a4160.speaker: A prominent Civilian Joint Task Force member (anonymous source)
a4160.name: A prominent Civilian Joint Task Force member (anonymous source)
a4160.speech: Said the new soldiers are not trusted: “To be insincere, I am a Civilian Joint Task Force member but I do not trust them. The military virtually leaves everything in their hands. They tell the military men when, how and where to go. Sometimes, if we go to the bush, the repentants will take a different path and won’t come back until after two days. And mind you, when they are going, they will do a lot of shopping, including foodstuffs. Where are they taking all the foodstuffs?” ; Said some have escaped with the new arms, and scores of them wish to return to the bush: “Some of them are also complaining that the government is not taking care of them; that the promises made to them were not fulfilled. There was also a case of about four of them escaping to the bush with arms and tricycles.”

a4160.speaker: International Centre for Investigative Reporting (report)
a4160.name: International Centre for Investigative Reporting (report)
a4160.speech: Reported how repentant terrorists were returning to the bush.

a4160.speaker: Nuhu Ribadu, National Security Adviser; Christopher Musa, Chief of Defence Staff; Olufemi Oluyede, Chief of Army Staff; Hassan Abubakar, Chief of Air Staff; and Abubakar Badaru, Minister of Defence
a4160.name: Nuhu Ribadu
a4160.title: National Security Adviser; Christopher Musa, Chief of Defence Staff; Olufemi Oluyede, Chief of Army Staff; Hassan Abubakar, Chief of Air Staff; and Abubakar Badaru, Minister of Defence
a4160.speech: Said the killings of the insurgents were a significant win in the war against insurgency in the North-east, and urged the troops to sustain the momentum.

a4160.speaker: Nuhu Ribadu, National Security Adviser
a4160.name: Nuhu Ribadu
a4160.title: National Security Adviser
a4160.speech: Noted that since President Bola Tinubu assumed office two years ago, over 13,543 Boko Haram elements were killed, while over 11,000 arms were recovered from terrorists; said 124,408 Boko Haram fighters and their families surrendered to troops; said that despite some setbacks, operations were ongoing in the Timbuktu Triangle, Tumbu islands, and other enclaves to smoke out the insurgents.

a4160.speaker: Amnesty International
a4160.name: Amnesty International
a4160.speech: Claimed over 10,000 people have been killed by non-state actors across Nigeria since Mr Tinubu assumed office.

a4160.speaker: Abubakar Badaru, Minister of Defence
a4160.name: Abubakar Badaru
a4160.title: Minister of Defence
a4160.speech: Speaking generally on security, said Nigeria was winning the war against terrorism; about the North-east and North-west regions said: “Markets are back. Farms are productive again. We have seen Fulani, Hausa, and other communities rebuilding trust. The progress is real and visible.”

a4160.speaker: Abdulsalam Abubakar, an army major-general and Theatre Commander of Operation Hadin Kai
a4160.name: Abdulsalam Abubakar
a4160.title: an army major-general and Theatre Commander of Operation Hadin Kai
a4160.speech: Said the infiltration of foreign mercenaries had significantly escalated the threat posed by terrorist groups like Boko Haram and ISWAP; revealed the arrest of four Pakistani nationals allegedly involved in arms running for the terrorists.

a4177.speaker: Mamoutou dit Djamba Sissoko, promoter of “Kanyela-Agri” fish-farming and market-gardening business
a4177.name: Mamoutou dit Djamba Sissoko
a4177.title: promoter of “Kanyela-Agri” fish-farming and market-gardening business
a4177.speech: Stresses that the soaring prices of fish feed are a major constraint for many fish farmers; by way of illustration mentions the 20 kg bag which currently costs 28,000 FCFA compared with 16,000 FCFA, and 40,000 FCFA for certain varieties ; reckons that with his 4 above-ground tanks he has to buy at least 20 kg of feed every week, and that this represents only the bare minimum required.

a4177.speaker: Mamoutou dit Djamba Sissoko, promoter of “Kanyela-Agri”
a4177.name: Mamoutou dit Djamba Sissoko
a4177.title: promoter of “Kanyela-Agri”
a4177.speech: Deplores the fact that locally produced feeds are not rich enough to allow good growth of the fish, which barely reach 700 g in 6 months, saying that with imported feeds one can obtain fish of more than 1 kg in 4 months ; makes an appeal to the State and its partners to set up a factory producing quality fish feed, and advocates better structuring of the actors concerned and optimal quality of subsidised inputs.

a4177.speaker: Madou Diarra, head of the “Kosso” fish farm
a4177.name: Madou Diarra
a4177.title: head of the “Kosso” fish farm
a4177.speech: “With the disappearance of certain fish species, there is a real enthusiasm for fish farming. Many people wish to go into this sector” ; says fish farming makes it possible to consume directly what one produces, while reducing fish imports ; stresses that with only 300,000 FCFA one can start fish farming on a small scale, a budget which allows the purchase of a 1 m3 above-ground tank, 105 fingerlings and several bags of feed.

a4177.speaker: Madou Diarra, head of the “Kosso” fish farm
a4177.name: Madou Diarra
a4177.title: head of the “Kosso” fish farm
a4177.speech: Deplores the fact that imported feeds remain costly and the absence of qualified specialists in fish pathology ; says that in the future he would like consumers to favour national production, and fish farmers to be able to meet consumer demand.

a4177.speaker: Mahamadou Kané, fish farmer
a4177.name: Mahamadou Kané
a4177.title: fish farmer
a4177.speech: Revealed that, in addition to having the appropriate broodstock, Mali possesses a significant number of hatcheries for the production of fingerlings, as well as producers of fish-farming inputs and fish feed.

a4177.speaker: Baréma Koïta, head of the fisheries sector of Ségou
a4177.name: Baréma Koïta
a4177.title: head of the fisheries sector of Ségou
a4177.speech: Said fish farming as a fish-rearing technique came into being in Mali with the establishment of a small experimental fish-farming station in the Region of San; the financing agreement instituting it was signed in November 1979 between the government of Mali and that of the United States with the support of USAID; thus an extension outpost was created at Niono, in the Office du Niger zone, because of the availability of water and agri-food by-products; he recalled that since then a multitude of techniques including rice-fish farming and cage fish farming have been tested and adapted in rural areas.

a4177.speaker: Baréma Koïta, head of the fisheries sector of Ségou
a4177.name: Baréma Koïta
a4177.title: head of the fisheries sector of Ségou
a4177.speech: Detailed that the Cercle of Ségou currently counts 131 ponds, 115 above-ground tanks and 2 floating cages; rice-fish farming covers 7,500 m2 while the ponds number 31 and extend over 51.68 hectares ; stressed that for a floating cage of 144 m3 the production obtained was 2,624 kg for 10,000 fingerlings, and the above-ground tank of 10 m3 with 1,000 fish made it possible to harvest 369 kg ; reported that among the initiatives under way to support fish farming in Ségou are the Degraded Land Restoration Project (PRTD), the project to support sustainable livelihoods and climate adaptation of fishing communities, and Jègè ni Jaba (JNJ).

a4177.speaker: Baréma Koïta, head of the fisheries sector of Ségou
a4177.name: Baréma Koïta
a4177.title: head of the fisheries sector of Ségou
a4177.speech: Said that the acquisition of inputs by producers remains a concern, that his structure does not have enough agents to cover the whole cercle, that access to certain localities is hampered by growing insecurity, and that the fisheries service of Ségou also faces insufficient financial means ; thinks that in order to benefit from fish farming it is necessary to “facilitate access to quality inputs at a reasonable price, have a permanent water source, regularly monitor the maintenance of the infrastructure and secure the facilities against theft” ; mentioned reducing the cost of inputs, the development of fish-farming infrastructure and capacity-building for producers as challenges and prospects.

a4325.speaker: Edem Wosornu, Director of Operations and Advocacy, UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a4325.name: Edem Wosornu
a4325.title: Director of Operations and Advocacy, UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a4325.speech: Warned on Wednesday at a UN Security Council meeting that more than 12 million people have been displaced inside and outside Sudan and more than 24 million Sudanese suffer acute hunger, and deplored: “The uninterrupted conflict in Sudan has inflicted immense suffering and turned parts of the country into a veritable hell.”

a4325.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) and Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a4325.name: World Food Programme (WFP) and Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a4325.speech: The main providers of humanitarian aid had to suspend their activities in the Zamzam refugee camp in North Darfur because of growing violence.

a4325.speaker: International community (humanitarian funding appeal)
a4325.name: International community (humanitarian funding appeal)
a4325.speech: Launched a funding appeal of 6 billion dollars for 2025 to support the humanitarian response, intended to help 21 million Sudanese inside the country and five million refugees in neighbouring countries.

a4816.speaker: Samuel Batcho, National Coordinator of MCA-Bénin II
a4816.name: Samuel Batcho
a4816.title: National Coordinator of MCA-Bénin II
a4816.speech: Said the programme’s entry into force is expected in the first quarter of 2017 ; “Since the last session, we have continued the process of putting the staff and the working framework in place. A first wave of staff is already installed. The processing of the second wave’s files is under way. We estimate that by the end of next October the staff will be complete.”

a4816.speaker: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, Minister of State in charge of Development and Chairman of the Board of MCA-Bénin II
a4816.name: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané
a4816.title: Minister of State in charge of Development and Chairman of the Board of MCA-Bénin II
a4816.speech: “This programme is important to us because it will allow us to lift the constraints linked to the availability of electrical energy in our country. Lifting these obstacles is an essential factor for boosting economic growth” ; reassured that the 4th session of the Board would produce resolutions marking the directors’ determination to move quickly toward entry into force.

a4851.speaker: Scott Bessent, United States Treasury Secretary
a4851.name: Scott Bessent
a4851.title: United States Treasury Secretary
a4851.speech: In an address to corporate America, his remarks sought to clarify President Donald Trump's sweeping economic measures—policies now widely referred to as Trump's "tariff war."

a4851.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a4851.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
a4851.title: Israeli Prime Minister
a4851.speech: Recently recommended Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize, crediting him for efforts to end the Israel–Gaza war, and formally submitted a nomination letter to the Nobel Committee in the Oval Office, praising Trump's peacemaking initiatives.

a4851.speaker: Hun Manet, Prime Minister of Cambodia
a4851.name: Hun Manet
a4851.title: Prime Minister of Cambodia
a4851.speech: Nominated Trump for the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, citing his role in halting armed conflict between Cambodia and Thailand after a territorial dispute displaced over 300,000 people.

a4851.speaker: Leaders of Cambodia and Thailand
a4851.name: Leaders of Cambodia and Thailand
a4851.speech: According to both countries' leaders, a phone call from Trump on July 26 broke the deadlock, leading to a Malaysia-brokered ceasefire on July 28.

a4851.speaker: Government of Cambodia (letter to the Norwegian Nobel Committee)
a4851.name: Government of Cambodia (letter to the Norwegian Nobel Committee)
a4851.speech: Praised Trump's "extraordinary statesmanship" and "visionary diplomacy," noting that his intervention prevented a potentially catastrophic war.

a4851.speaker: Ilham Aliyev, President of Azerbaijan
a4851.name: Ilham Aliyev
a4851.title: President of Azerbaijan
a4851.speech: Credited Trump's diplomacy for the peace deal signed at the White House and stated, "Who, if not President Trump, deserves a Nobel Peace Prize?"

a4851.speaker: Nikol Pashinyan, Prime Minister of Armenia
a4851.name: Nikol Pashinyan
a4851.title: Prime Minister of Armenia
a4851.speech: Credited Trump's diplomacy for the peace deal and echoed, "He has earned it."

a4851.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4851.name: Donald Trump
a4851.title: US President
a4851.speech: His view is that the new tariffs are fundamentally reciprocal, designed to end unfair trade practices against the U.S.; the point of introducing new rules and deadlines, he argues, is to secure compliance—not to punish unnecessarily.

a4851.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4851.name: Donald Trump
a4851.title: US President
a4851.speech: Issued deadlines for Iran to negotiate an end to its suspected nuclear enrichment program, warning of dire consequences.

a4851.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4851.name: Donald Trump
a4851.title: US President
a4851.speech: Issued Russia an ultimatum to end its more than three-year war against Ukraine.

a4851.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4851.name: Donald Trump
a4851.title: US President
a4851.speech: Called on Hamas to release the hostages taken during its 2023 incursion into Israel so that the Israeli siege on Palestine could end.

a4851.speaker: Dmitry Medvedev, former Russian President, now in charge of Russia's war arsenal
a4851.name: Dmitry Medvedev
a4851.title: former Russian President, now in charge of Russia's war arsenal
a4851.speech: Appeared to issue a veiled threat to the U.S. in response to the new deadline set by the Trump administration for Russia to end the war.

a4851.speaker: Roger Fisher and William Ury, "Getting to Yes: Negotiating Agreement Without Giving In"
a4851.name: Roger Fisher and William Ury
a4851.title: "Getting to Yes: Negotiating Agreement Without Giving In"
a4851.speech: Emphasizes that a good agreement leaves no party feeling cheated—that a win–win outcome, one that meets the needs of all parties, is ideal.

a4851.speaker: France, the United Kingdom and Canada (government announcements)
a4851.name: France
a4851.title: the United Kingdom and Canada (government announcements)
a4851.speech: Announced they will recognize Palestine as a nation, a departure from the traditional Western stance of withholding recognition.

a4919.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4919.name: Donald Trump
a4919.title: US President
a4919.speech: Said he expects his ally Elon Musk to find billions of dollars of fraud and abuse at the Pentagon: “We're going to find billions, hundreds of millions of dollars of fraud and abuse,” Trump said of the largest federal department in an interview with Fox News ; “And, you know, the people elected me on that.” ; seemed to double down on the idea, saying he was going to ask Musk “very soon, like maybe in 24 hours, to go check the Department of Education. … Then I'm going to go, go to the military”.

a4919.speaker: Mike Waltz, US National Security Advisor
a4919.name: Mike Waltz
a4919.title: US National Security Advisor
a4919.speech: Suggested in a separate interview on Sunday that the Pentagon's shipbuilding processes could be an area of particular interest: “Everything there seems to cost too much, take too long and deliver too little to the soldiers… We do need business leaders to go in there and absolutely reform the Pentagon's acquisition process,” Waltz said in an interview with NBC News.

a4919.speaker: Chris Murphy, US Senator (Democrat)
a4919.name: Chris Murphy
a4919.title: US Senator (Democrat)
a4919.speech: Warned of an “assault on the Constitution” and said Trump was ushering in a “billionaire takeover of government”: “The president wants to be able to decide how and where money is spent so that he can reward his political friends, he can punish his political enemies. That is the evisceration of democracy,” Murphy told ABC News.

a4919.speaker: US judge (unnamed)
a4919.name: US judge (unnamed)
a4919.speech: Issued an emergency order on Saturday blocking DOGE from accessing Treasury Department payment systems that contain Americans' sensitive data.

a4990.speaker: Abida Mia, Malawi Minister of Water and Sanitation
a4990.name: Abida Mia
a4990.title: Malawi Minister of Water and Sanitation
a4990.speech: Has urged the tea sector to embrace value-addition for the country to reap more benefits: "While we take pride in Malawi's rich tea history, the future demands that we evolve. It is time to focus on value-addi tion—moving beyond simply producing raw tea and investing in processes such as blending, packaging, and branding within Malawi itself." ; She also called for collaboration among tea sector players to propel Malawi tea onto the global stage: "Together we can invest in both branding and value-added processes that can propel Malawian tea onto the global stage."

a4990.speaker: Sangwani Hara, Tea Association of Malawi chairperson
a4990.name: Sangwani Hara
a4990.title: Tea Association of Malawi chairperson
a4990.speech: Said his association believes that trade pacts and enhanced trade can provide a good alternative to aid and development assistance: "With increased tea imports from Malawi, British tea drinkers will be allowed to consume a great product at a fair price while contributing to Malawi's and tea estates' foreign exchange earnings and development agenda."

a4990.speaker: Thomas Bisika, Malawi High Commissioner
a4990.name: Thomas Bisika
a4990.title: Malawi High Commissioner
a4990.speech: Said tea will play a significant role as Malawi transitions from aid to trade.

a4990.speaker: Thomas Bisika, Malawi High Commissioner
a4990.name: Thomas Bisika
a4990.title: Malawi High Commissioner
a4990.speech: Thanked Sureena Brackenridge, MP, and Warinder Juss, MP, for hosting the event.

a4990.speaker: Sheikh Aliur Rahman, London Tea Exchange chief executive officer
a4990.name: Sheikh Aliur Rahman
a4990.title: London Tea Exchange chief executive officer
a4990.speech: Called for fair play in the tea production chain.

a4998.speaker: Public Health Institute of Malawi (Phim), daily update
a4998.name: Public Health Institute of Malawi (Phim)
a4998.title: daily update
a4998.speech: Reported three new cases of Mpox, bringing the number of recorded infections to 15 since the outbreak was declared on April 16 2025, and that the new cases have pushed the number of affected districts to three, all of which have reported cases within the past 42 days; according to the update, only one patient is currently admitted to a treatment facility, while no new discharges have been registered in the latest notice.

a4998.speaker: Public Health Institute of Malawi (Phim), statement
a4998.name: Public Health Institute of Malawi (Phim)
a4998.title: statement
a4998.speech: Recently suggested that a majority of the patients were aged between 17 and 41, and said in a statement last week: "Investigations are underway to establish the possible source of infection and trace contacts."

a4998.speaker: Richard Mvula, Lilongwe district health office spokesperson (quoted in The Guardian)
a4998.name: Richard Mvula
a4998.title: Lilongwe district health office spokesperson (quoted in The Guardian)
a4998.speech: "A commonality about these cases is that some were immune-compromised."

a4998.speaker: The Guardian (UK) report
a4998.name: The Guardian (UK) report
a4998.speech: According to the report, patients who were on antiretroviral therapy (ART) had been forced to stop taking their medication because of drug shortages.

a4998.speaker: George Jobe, Malawi Health Equity Network (Mhen) executive director
a4998.name: George Jobe
a4998.title: Malawi Health Equity Network (Mhen) executive director
a4998.speech: Described the situation as worrisome and stressed the need for all stakeholders to engage an extra gear to curb the viral infection: "For instance, we should analyse if there are similarities in the people who are testing positive, such as economic status, social status, urban versus rural among other parameters. This will help to determine if the surge is as a result of limited knowledge among the public or other things." ; He also highlighted the need to publicise the numbers of cases in the media so that people are reminded about the problem amidst us.

a4998.speaker: Ministry of Health of Malawi
a4998.name: Ministry of Health of Malawi
a4998.speech: Has reiterated its call for vigilance and early reporting of symptoms as part of efforts to contain the spread of the virus.

a5089.speaker: Local Tunisian press
a5089.name: Local Tunisian press
a5089.speech: According to the local press, nine Tunisian members of the flotilla returned to Tunisia on Sunday after being released by the Israeli authorities.

a5089.speaker: Tunisian media
a5089.name: Tunisian media
a5089.speech: According to Tunisian media, the group was welcomed by hundreds of people, including members of their families, journalists and representatives of civil society.

a5162.speaker: Zambia’s Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development
a5162.name: Zambia’s Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development
a5162.speech: Has outlined the vast critical mineral opportunities available across the country in a report released in collaboration with the British Geological Survey.

a5162.speaker: Report by Zambia’s Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development in collaboration with the British Geological Survey
a5162.name: Report by Zambia’s Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development in collaboration with the British Geological Survey
a5162.speech: Covering strategic minerals such as copper, cobalt, manganese and more, the report underscores the instrumental role the country already plays in global supply chains.

a5283.speaker: Tanzania Premier League Board
a5283.name: Tanzania Premier League Board
a5283.speech: Announced the postponement of the match a few hours before kick-off; in its statement announcing the postponement the League Board contradicted itself, because the rules for postponing a match are set out in League Regulation No. 34 and none of them states that if a team has been prevented from training the match will not be played.

a5283.speaker: Simba SC (statement)
a5283.name: Simba SC (statement)
a5283.speech: Issued a statement boycotting the match because they had been prevented from holding their final training session at the Mkapa stadium by people alleged to be Yanga "commandos".

a5283.speaker: Yanga SC (public statement)
a5283.name: Yanga SC (public statement)
a5283.speech: Has already said it will not play the rescheduled match and has decided to go and demand its rights at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) because the fixture was postponed without regard to the existing regulations, claiming the three points from the March 8 match.

a5283.speaker: Jamal Osman and Nahom Tesfaye, football scouts from Sweden
a5283.name: Jamal Osman and Nahom Tesfaye
a5283.title: football scouts from Sweden
a5283.speech: Said that missing the derby cost them more than 20 million shillings (7,619 dollars) spent on the trip from Sweden to Tanzania, costs including food, transport and accommodation; they said they will still continue to follow Mzize's progress.

a5283.speaker: Jamal Osman, football scout from Sweden
a5283.name: Jamal Osman
a5283.title: football scout from Sweden
a5283.speech: "We planned for a long time, we set aside other work so that we could watch Mzize in a big match. Now we have left without achieving our goal," said Osman with regret at Julius Nyerere International Airport ; "We will try to follow him by other means, but this opportunity was the best for us."

a5283.speaker: Nahom Tesfaye, football scout from Sweden
a5283.name: Nahom Tesfaye
a5283.title: football scout from Sweden
a5283.speech: "We have lost a lot of time and money, but these are football matters. We have to move on."

a5283.speaker: Juma Athumani, sports-viewing kiosk owner in Kinyerezi
a5283.name: Juma Athumani
a5283.title: sports-viewing kiosk owner in Kinyerezi
a5283.speech: Said he spent more than 150,000 shillings improving his place but did not recover even a quarter of those costs: "I rented a big screen and bought new speakers so that Yanga and Simba fans could enjoy the match, but now everything has been ruined. The money has been lost for nothing."

a5283.speaker: Another sports-viewing kiosk owner in Mabibo (unnamed)
a5283.name: Another sports-viewing kiosk owner in Mabibo (unnamed)
a5283.speech: Said he had paid for Azam decoders as well as buying drinks to sell during the match, but everything went wrong and he does not know who can ease his pain: "It is true that even though the match has been postponed, the drinks and the decoders will remain, but it was not my aim to spend extra money on preparations for that match, and you know our Tanzanian incomes are patched together - you put out money by calculation in order to reap a profit, but things have turned sour for me. It hurts."

a5283.speaker: Jesca Manji, die-hard Yanga fan and food vendor (mama lishe)
a5283.name: Jesca Manji
a5283.title: die-hard Yanga fan and food vendor (mama lishe)
a5283.speech: Said the postponement of the derby plunged her into debts that nearly drove her to harm herself: "I took chickens worth 2 million shillings and I made all the business preparations, everything was ready, and surprisingly the Tanzania Premier League Board announced at 2 p.m. that there was no match. I found myself drained of strength, unable to know what to do, because the owner of the chickens wants his money, not words" ; "I found myself wanting to drink poison so I would die, but the thing that gave me strength is that I am a mother raising my children by myself; I thought about how they would live if I left this world, and I got the strength to keep fighting to see how I will pay people's debts" ; "TFF and the League Board should have thought broadly in their decision; they know there are women traders who are fighting for their lives - let me keep quiet, because I am angry and I don't know what to do."

a5283.speaker: Other vendors alongside the Mkapa Stadium
a5283.name: Other vendors alongside the Mkapa Stadium
a5283.speech: Said they expected to make extra money through the derby as always happens when there is a big match, but found themselves suffering losses of food with no idea who would pay them those costs.

a5283.speaker: Hellen Muro, food vendor (mama ntilie)
a5283.name: Hellen Muro
a5283.title: food vendor (mama ntilie)
a5283.speech: "It hurts a lot that a few people do things at their own whim, without caring about the losses suffered by those behind a big match like this; it is disrespecting the fans and football as a whole, because I hear that no postponement regulations were used, only decisions to protect one another - this is not right and it sets back the economy of individuals and even of the nation as a whole."

a5283.speaker: Getruda Emmanuel, fan from Mafinga
a5283.name: Getruda Emmanuel
a5283.title: fan from Mafinga
a5283.speech: Said the derby really punished them, as they travelled from Mafinga to Dar es Salaam in two hired coaster vehicles as a group of 60 fans, each paying 60,000 shillings for the round trip, plus 20,000 shillings a day for two days of accommodation: "We contributed among ourselves, each one paid 60,000 shillings for the round-trip fare, we hired two vehicles and we were 60 fans. If you look at the costs of hiring all those vehicles, the total fare was three million six hundred thousand shillings" ; "Forget those costs; I am also a trader, I had to close my business for two days in order to come and watch this match, so I have not brought in anything and the thing I came for I missed" ; "Because of what is going on, I don't think that in future we fans from the regions will come to watch these derbies or any big match, because it has become uncertain whether it will be played."

a5283.speaker: Yanga SC leadership (non-response)
a5283.name: Yanga SC leadership (non-response)
a5283.speech: Mwanaspoti sought out the Yanga leadership to find out the losses suffered by the club, but their phones rang without being answered.

a5283.speaker: Internal source from Yanga club (anonymous)
a5283.name: Internal source from Yanga club (anonymous)
a5283.speech: "You cannot get them now, because they are in discussions and making a joint assessment to determine the full loss so that it can be put into the legal letter that will be sent to CAS, in order to claim the three points of the March 8 match as set out in the public statement" ; "There are big costs that were incurred starting from camp preparations, advertising and other things, so it is not easy to know them; that is why they are meeting now to settle it and then they will issue a statement, but the truth is that Yanga has suffered losses of millions of shillings because of the selfishness of a few."

a5283.speaker: Ally Kamwe, Yanga Information Officer
a5283.name: Ally Kamwe
a5283.title: Yanga Information Officer
a5283.speech: Was quoted as saying that before the match was postponed more than 40,000 tickets had already been sold to fans, who did not get the chance to witness the fixture.

a5283.speaker: Simba officials and League Board officials (non-response)
a5283.name: Simba officials and League Board officials (non-response)
a5283.speech: Efforts to reach Simba officials and those of the League Board to obtain clarification on the losses they incurred in preparing for the match bore no fruit, as their phones rang without being answered.

a5419.speaker: Marie Chantal Nijimbere, Burundian Minister in charge of Trade
a5419.name: Marie Chantal Nijimbere
a5419.title: Burundian Minister in charge of Trade
a5419.speech: “The objective of the Simplified Trade Regime is to promote the development of cross-border trade by allowing the small goods of small traders to benefit from the elimination of customs duties and from the preferential treatment of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (Comesa) on the goods that appear on the common list.” ; specified that Recos is a programme launched by Comesa with a view to helping small cross-border traders who trade in small quantities of goods, so that they can orient their activities with the aim of simplifying customs clearance processes and reducing the costs of commercial transactions ; indicated that, according to the trade agreement signed between the two parties, the common list of products is not final and will be subject to revision every six months with a view to regular self-evaluation in a spirit of win-win partnership, before calling for an increase in the production of the goods concerned in order to have sufficient quantities to export and benefit from this Recos.

a5419.speaker: Two cross-border traders (one Burundian, one Congolese) representing women traders
a5419.name: Two cross-border traders (one Burundian
a5419.title: one Congolese) representing women traders
a5419.speech: In their testimonies warmly welcomed the launch of Recos, long and impatiently awaited; specified that it will make it possible to resolve quite a few of the challenges they faced in their work, and that Recos will allow an increase in revenue and a saving of time; also requested regular monitoring of the implementation of this Recos, and the translation of the texts governing this regime into three languages, namely Kirundi, French and Swahili, to facilitate their understanding.

a5419.speaker: Minister Marie Chantal Nijimbere and her Congolese counterpart in charge of foreign trade
a5419.name: Minister Marie Chantal Nijimbere and her Congolese counterpart in charge of foreign trade
a5419.speech: Reassured them, promising them regular follow-up, because this Recos results from the will of the highest authorities of the two countries; called on all the services working at the border posts to do everything possible so that the implementation of this Simplified Trade Regime is crowned with success.

a5435.speaker: Anna, Mpox survivor in Uganda
a5435.name: Anna
a5435.title: Mpox survivor in Uganda
a5435.speech: Recalls: “I had body aches, particularly in the joints. Sometimes I felt too much heat in my body. My eyes were red and I could not eat because of the sores in my mouth.”

a5435.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a5435.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a5435.speech: Declared Mpox a public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC) on 14 August 2024.

a5435.speaker: Uganda Ministry of Health (reports)
a5435.name: Uganda Ministry of Health (reports)
a5435.speech: As of 18 December 2024, Ministry of Health reports show that 1,089 cumulative cases of mpox have been confirmed in Uganda.

a5435.speaker: Bernard Ikwaras, Mpox disease surveillance officer for Pallisa district
a5435.name: Bernard Ikwaras
a5435.title: Mpox disease surveillance officer for Pallisa district
a5435.speech: Stressed during the community dialogue the need to avoid stigmatising people with the disease and survivors: “Anyone can catch Mpox. It is therefore important that, as a community, we support one another. When people recover from Mpox, they can no longer spread the disease, so it is in our interest to welcome them back into the community.”

a5435.speaker: Dr Charles Njuguna, WHO acting representative in Uganda
a5435.name: Dr Charles Njuguna
a5435.title: WHO acting representative in Uganda
a5435.speech: “From Anna’s experience, it is essential to raise more public awareness about Mpox and to ensure that all health workers in public and private health centres in the country take part in webinars and capacity-building sessions.” ; “This will facilitate rapid diagnosis and the start of the recommended treatment and other control interventions to stop the spread of Mpox in the country.”

a5603.speaker: Ministry of Health of Malawi
a5603.name: Ministry of Health of Malawi
a5603.speech: Says there are about 46 000 HIV-positive Malawians who do not know their status and are consequently not on antiretroviral therapy (ART), raising concerns about spread of new infections.

a5603.speaker: Rabson Kachala, deputy director of the Ministry of Health's HIV and Viral Hepatitis Directorate
a5603.name: Rabson Kachala
a5603.title: deputy director of the Ministry of Health's HIV and Viral Hepatitis Directorate
a5603.speech: Said the figure is based on data captured during a quarterly supervision exercise conducted in March this year across 800 health facilities; said that while 991 000 people in Malawi have tested HIV positive, only around 945 000 are currently accessing ART ; "This is a significant treatment gap. Many of the individuals who are not on ART fear stigma and discrimination which keeps them away from health facilities. This is a serious public health concern" ; called for more aggressive public sensitisation to encourage people to know their HIV status and seek treatment early.

a5603.speaker: Rabson Kachala, deputy director of the Ministry of Health's HIV and Viral Hepatitis Directorate
a5603.name: Rabson Kachala
a5603.title: deputy director of the Ministry of Health's HIV and Viral Hepatitis Directorate
a5603.speech: Stressed that access to ART remains uninterrupted despite the ongoing restrictions on some donor-funded activities: "There are misconceptions that ARVs are not available, but that is not true. These drugs are procured through the Global Fund and remain fully stocked. People should collect their medication on their scheduled dates without fear" ; according to Kachala, the government has increased domestic financing for HIV programming in the 2025/26 financial year to K3.4 billion, including K1 billion for ART co-financing, K2.4 billion for sample transportation, and K500 million for capacity building.

a5603.speaker: David Kamkwamba, executive director of the Network of Journalists Living with HIV
a5603.name: David Kamkwamba
a5603.title: executive director of the Network of Journalists Living with HIV
a5603.speech: Appealed to the media to take an active role in raising public awareness about Malawi's HIV response and the evolving funding landscape: "The media must help break the silence and reduce stigma by consistently covering issues around HIV treatment, prevention and sustainable financing" ; said continued misinformation about ARV availability, coupled with low community engagement, risks eroding years of progress made in the fight against HIV in Malawi.

a5603.speaker: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda, Minister of Health
a5603.name: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda
a5603.title: Minister of Health
a5603.speech: Announced in 2022 that Malawi had surpassed the United Nations Aids Agency (UNAids) 95-95-95 HIV epidemic control targets ahead of the deadline in June 2025.

a5603.speaker: Statistics (cited)
a5603.name: Statistics (cited)
a5603.speech: The statistics show that Malawi is now at 94:99:95, meaning that 94 percent of all people with HIV are aware of their status, 99 percent of those aware of their status are on ART and 95 percent of those on antiretroviral treatment have achieved viral load suppression.

a5646.speaker: Joe Biden, President of the United States
a5646.name: Joe Biden
a5646.title: President of the United States
a5646.speech: Called on Hamas on Tuesday to accept a Gaza ceasefire deal by the Muslim holy month of Ramadan; warned Hamas to agree to a truce by Ramadan: “There’s got to be a ceasefire because Ramadan - if we get into circumstances where this continues to Ramadan, Israel and Jerusalem could be very, very dangerous.”

a5646.speaker: Hamas (Palestinian militant group)
a5646.name: Hamas (Palestinian militant group)
a5646.speech: Warned that talks for a truce and hostage release cannot go on “indefinitely”.

a5646.speaker: Kamala Harris, US Vice President
a5646.name: Kamala Harris
a5646.title: US Vice President
a5646.speech: Has expressed “deep concern about the humanitarian conditions in Gaza”.

a5646.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a5646.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a5646.speech: Has reported children dying of starvation in two northern Gaza hospitals; said an aid mission at the weekend found that 10 children had died of starvation at the Al-Awda and Kamal Adwan hospitals.

a5646.speaker: Al-Qahera News (Egyptian outlet close to intelligence services)
a5646.name: Al-Qahera News (Egyptian outlet close to intelligence services)
a5646.speech: Said the talks would continue for a fourth consecutive day on Wednesday.

a5646.speaker: Antony Blinken, US Secretary of State
a5646.name: Antony Blinken
a5646.title: US Secretary of State
a5646.speech: Urged Hamas to accept an “immediate ceasefire”.

a5646.speaker: Israeli government
a5646.name: Israeli government
a5646.speech: Said it would allow Muslim worshippers access to Al-Aqsa during Ramadan “in similar numbers to those in previous years”.

a5646.speaker: Israeli media
a5646.name: Israeli media
a5646.speech: Reporting that Israeli delegates had boycotted the Cairo talks after Hamas failed to provide a list of living hostages.

a5646.speaker: Bassem Naim, senior Hamas leader
a5646.name: Bassem Naim
a5646.title: senior Hamas leader
a5646.speech: Told AFP that details on the prisoners “were not mentioned in any documents or proposals circulated during the negotiation process”.

a5646.speaker: Osama Hamdan, Hamas official in Beirut
a5646.name: Osama Hamdan
a5646.title: Hamas official in Beirut
a5646.speech: Said his group would “not allow the path of negotiations to be open indefinitely”.

a5646.speaker: Israel (government)
a5646.name: Israel (government)
a5646.speech: Has said it believes 130 of the 250 captives taken by Hamas fighters in their 7 October attack remain in Gaza but that 31 have been killed.

a5646.speaker: Jake Sullivan, US National Security Advisor, and Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani
a5646.name: Jake Sullivan
a5646.title: US National Security Advisor, and Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani
a5646.speech: Met and agreed that “the release of sick, wounded, elderly, and women hostages would result in an immediate ceasefire in Gaza over a period of at least six weeks”.

a5646.speaker: White House (readout of the meeting)
a5646.name: White House (readout of the meeting)
a5646.speech: Said the first phase of a ceasefire would enable “a surge of humanitarian assistance to the people of Gaza and provide time and space to secure more enduring arrangements and sustained calm”.

a5646.speaker: Nader Abu Shanab, resident of Khan Yunis
a5646.name: Nader Abu Shanab
a5646.title: resident of Khan Yunis
a5646.speech: Said, pointing to the rubble with blackened hands: “We want to eat and live. Take a look at our homes. How am I to blame, a single, unarmed person without any income in this impoverished country?”

a5646.speaker: Jordan
a5646.name: Jordan
a5646.speech: Said French and Egyptian planes also took part in the airdrop operation.

a5646.speaker: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a5646.name: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a5646.speech: Said Israeli troops turned away an aid convoy at a checkpoint leading to northern Gaza and that it was later looted “by desperate people”.

a5646.speaker: AFP tally based on official Israeli figures
a5646.name: AFP tally based on official Israeli figures
a5646.speech: The Hamas attack on southern Israel on 7 October resulted in about 1,160 deaths, most of them civilians.

a5646.speaker: Health ministry in the Hamas-ruled territory
a5646.name: Health ministry in the Hamas-ruled territory
a5646.speech: Israel’s retaliatory offensive has killed more than 30,600 people, mostly women and children.

a5646.speaker: United Nations (report published Monday)
a5646.name: United Nations (report published Monday)
a5646.speech: Said there were “reasonable grounds to believe” rapes were committed and that hostages taken to Gaza had also been raped.

a5646.speaker: Israel (government)
a5646.name: Israel (government)
a5646.speech: Has accused the UN of taking too long to respond to the claims and recalled its UN Ambassador Gilad Erdan shortly after the report’s release.

a5646.speaker: US military / US Central Command (statement)
a5646.name: US military / US Central Command (statement)
a5646.speech: Said it shot down three drones and a missile fired toward one of its destroyers in the Red Sea by Huthi rebels in Yemen on Tuesday: “one anti-ship ballistic missile and three one-way attack unmanned aerial systems” had been shot down and its ship, the USS Carney, was undamaged.

a5646.speaker: Iran-backed Houthis
a5646.name: Iran-backed Houthis
a5646.speech: Saying they were hitting Israel-linked vessels in support of Palestinians in Gaza.

a5743.speaker: Dr. Dominic Akuritinga Ayine, Attorney General of Ghana
a5743.name: Dr. Dominic Akuritinga Ayine
a5743.title: Attorney General of Ghana
a5743.speech: Has dismissed claims that President John Dramani Mahama influenced his decision to discontinue several high-profile criminal cases; speaking at a press conference in Accra on Wednesday, February 12, clarified that these decisions were made independently by his office after a thorough professional review of the cases and emphasized that President Mahama played no role in the discontinuation of any case; maintains that his decisions were legally and ethically sound, reiterating that justice, not politics, guided his actions.

a5743.speaker: Dr. Dominic Akuritinga Ayine, Attorney General of Ghana
a5743.name: Dr. Dominic Akuritinga Ayine
a5743.title: Attorney General of Ghana
a5743.speech: On the reasons for terminating the trials: "Ladies and gentlemen, my decision to terminate the criminal trials was animated in the main by three factors. The first was that for ethical and professional reasons, I could not in good conscience continue to prosecute some of the cases," he said. "The second was that, for some of the cases, my own review and analysis of the charges showed clearly that the charges were defective, and some were filed against the promptings of plain commonsense." ; "The third reason was that, in some of the cases, the evidence led so far showed that there was reasonable doubt as to the guilt of the accused persons, and no prosecutor should continue to pursue a case in the face of overwhelming doubt regarding the guilt of the accused."

a5743.speaker: Dr. Dominic Akuritinga Ayine, Attorney General of Ghana
a5743.name: Dr. Dominic Akuritinga Ayine
a5743.title: Attorney General of Ghana
a5743.speech: On the process of consultation: explained that before reaching these decisions, he conducted extensive consultations, including multiple briefings with the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) and discussions with defence lawyers involved in the cases; further noted that in cases where disagreements arose - such as those related to the banking sector clean-up - he communicated his views directly to the lawyers involved.

a5743.speaker: Dr. Dominic Akuritinga Ayine, Attorney General of Ghana
a5743.name: Dr. Dominic Akuritinga Ayine
a5743.title: Attorney General of Ghana
a5743.speech: On his constitutional prosecutorial powers: "As Attorney General, I am keenly aware that the prosecutorial authority vested in me under Article 88 of the Constitution is discretionary in nature and is subject to the constitutional requirements set out in Article 296 of the Constitution." ; "The import of these constitutional requirements is that, in the exercise of my prosecutorial power, I must not only act reasonably and fairly and comply with all the requirements imposed on me by law but also, I must be candid with those whose life and liberty depend on my decisions."

a5743.speaker: Dr. Dominic Akuritinga Ayine, Attorney General of Ghana
a5743.name: Dr. Dominic Akuritinga Ayine
a5743.title: Attorney General of Ghana
a5743.speech: On the SSNIT and banking sector cases: noted that some persons linked to SSNIT and the banking sector cases were still standing trial.

a5764.speaker: Marie Harf, spokesperson for the US State Department
a5764.name: Marie Harf
a5764.title: spokesperson for the US State Department
a5764.speech: Recalled that over the past summer the State Department notified Congress of how it intended to fund certain programmes in Pakistan, as part of a long process of “restarting our security assistance”, and added that the $350 million counterterrorism financial assistance serves to develop “the capacities of Pakistan’s security forces in counter-insurgency and counter-terrorism” ; specified: “For budget year 2014, the president asked Congress for foreign aid to Pakistan in the amount of 1.162 billion dollars, of which 857 million is civilian aid and 305 million is security assistance.”

a5805.speaker: Sylvestre Amoussou, Beninese film director
a5805.name: Sylvestre Amoussou
a5805.title: Beninese film director
a5805.speech: justified this by the need to make Beninese towns known beyond the borders ; “...when I speak of humanitarian aid, I show that even the aid they give for the African continent, part of it is already embezzled by the donors before it arrives. And when it arrives in Africa, our governments embezzle a large part and the people it is meant for get very little. It is a wake-up call to speak about good governance, which is really very difficult, whether at home or elsewhere.”

a5805.speaker: Berthold Hinkati, Director of the cultural space Le Centre
a5805.name: Berthold Hinkati
a5805.title: Director of the cultural space Le Centre
a5805.speech: “There was quality and it denounced social phenomena. That fits well with the Wà Cinéma programme. Hence the idea of a screening with this same director who does honour to Africa and to Benin. Directors in general take advantage of fiction to convey very good messages. And this evening we heard very good information about corruption. We really saw the underside of corruption.”

a5805.speaker: Joël Hossou, user of the cultural space Le Centre
a5805.name: Joël Hossou
a5805.title: user of the cultural space Le Centre
a5805.speech: said it is not easy to deal with this kind of subject and that it took Sylvestre Amoussou a great deal of daring and courage ; “The film was shot in 2010 and with that quality, I imagine he must take up a similar project now. I believe it will be of very good quality. I hope people have learned from the film and may corruption diminish in African communities.”

a5805.speaker: Terrence Anago, film director
a5805.name: Terrence Anago
a5805.title: film director
a5805.speech: says he appreciates the technique, the story, the dramaturgy; in his words, it is always a pleasure to come and view quality works at the cultural space Le Centre.

a6045.speaker: Ben Nangombe, Executive Director of the Ministry of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a6045.name: Ben Nangombe
a6045.title: Executive Director of the Ministry of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a6045.speech: Reiterated that Namibia has made commendable progress in curbing the spread of infectious diseases like HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, and malaria: “We have witnessed significant forward movement in achieving the goals articulated in the National Strategic Framework, thanks in large part to the invaluable support by our Development Cooperation Partners and the active role of Civil Society Organisations (CSOs). The data and figures towards Namibia's achievements of the UNAIDS 95-95-95 fast-tracked targets for HIV are well known to all of you. As of 2022 in Namibia, 94% of HIV-positive individuals know their status, 97% of them are on antiretroviral therapy (ART), and 93% have reached viral suppression (94-97-93)” ; “This is the last mile, and we dare not relent. We will not falter. Not now, when we have achieved so much. Let us maintain the momentum and deliver a solid NOP and a comprehensive sustainability framework to operationalise our NSF for HIV, TB, malaria, and hepatitis.”

a6045.speaker: Cheryl Amoroso, PEPFAR Representative
a6045.name: Cheryl Amoroso
a6045.title: PEPFAR Representative
a6045.speech: Discussed the funding perspective of PEPFAR as a donor: “From a PEPFAR perspective, we need to already embrace change to together understand the transformation of HIV programming in line with this developing vision that the country has for its future health system, not just from an HIV perspective but holistically. From a donor viewpoint, we are ready to adapt our investments to help realise this developing vision, which is why today and tomorrow are so important. We will use this roadmap to guide our investment. The Namibia PEPFAR investments have already started making shifts better aligned with the future vision that is already developing, and the clarity that we will have on this documentation will continue to support that transition.”

a6142.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a6142.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a6142.title: President of Malawi
a6142.speech: Acknowledged his defeat in the general elections of 16 September and congratulated his predecessor Peter Mutharika ; speaking from the Kamuzu Palace in Lilongwe, he admitted that Mutharika held a lead he described as “insurmountable” after the counting of 24 councils, with only 12 remaining ; “A moment ago, I called Professor Mutharika directly to congratulate him on his historic victory and to wish him good luck as the new president of the Republic of Malawi” ; calling for national unity, the outgoing head of state invited all citizens, whatever their political affiliations, to rally behind the president-elect.

a6142.speaker: Billy Gamah, President of the Malawi Council of Churches (MCC)
a6142.name: Billy Gamah
a6142.title: President of the Malawi Council of Churches (MCC)
a6142.speech: Had stated that a rapid concession would constitute “an act of statesmanship” fostering calm and maturity among supporters.

a6142.speaker: Bakili Muluzi, former President of Malawi
a6142.name: Bakili Muluzi
a6142.title: former President of Malawi
a6142.speech: Had encouraged Chakwera to “let the country move forward” and recalled that “there is life after the Presidential Palace.”

a6142.speaker: Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC) (provisional figures)
a6142.name: Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC) (provisional figures)
a6142.speech: According to provisional figures published by the Electoral Commission (MEC), Peter Mutharika was gathering around 66% of valid votes, against 24% for Lazarus Chakwera, with 205,480 ballots declared void, that is 3.45%.

a6293.speaker: Jackline Uwaya, representative of the USAID Afya Yangu Southern Zone project
a6293.name: Jackline Uwaya
a6293.title: representative of the USAID Afya Yangu Southern Zone project
a6293.speech: Said that the community has a great contribution in the fight to eradicate and end gender violence. “Together we have the ability to influence the society mindset towards gender violence, as people take time to think deeply about any information about acts of gender-based violence when they occur,” said Uwaya ; she added that if members of society, government and other stakeholders join forces, GBV will end ; she said that currently Tanzania has been able to take major steps in the fight against gender violence compared to previous years, thanks to the cooperation between the government and private institutions.

a6293.speaker: Ambassador Getrude Mongela, chief guest and gender activist
a6293.name: Ambassador Getrude Mongela
a6293.title: chief guest and gender activist
a6293.speech: Said that if society is properly educated about the effects of gender-based violence, it will refrain from such actions. “These acts of violence against gender occur in the society in which we all live. If we invest a lot on promoting education and we all join together, these actions can end completely,” said Ambassador Mongela ; according to the gender activist, it is possible to have a zero gender-based violence society, hence members of the community should join forces in the GBV fight. “Everyone should fulfill their responsibility in ensuring that sexual violence is eradicated,” she insisted.

a6474.speaker: Namibian government
a6474.name: Namibian government
a6474.speech: Says the imposition of reciprocal tariffs by the US President, Donald Trump, requires a balanced approach from Southern African Customs Union member states, including Namibia, to find a workable solution.

a6474.speaker: Ministry of International Relations and Trade of Namibia (statement)
a6474.name: Ministry of International Relations and Trade of Namibia (statement)
a6474.speech: Says that to mitigate the impact of the tariffs imposed, stakeholder engagements will be imperative to gauge and establish the extent of the effects imposed by the U.S. ; “It is also worth noting that the imposition of tariffs could lead to decreased competitiveness of Namibian beef and fish exports in the U.S. market, potentially reducing sales volume and demand for Namibian products due to price increases attributed to the tariff. Overall, the tariffs could disrupt established supply chains and negatively affect Namibia’s export earnings, impacting broader preferential stability for Namibian products under the Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) regime,” the statement reads.

a6474.speaker: Ministry of International Relations and Trade of Namibia (on Namibia’s own tariffs)
a6474.name: Ministry of International Relations and Trade of Namibia (on Namibia’s own tariffs)
a6474.speech: Labels the 42% tariff Namibia imposes on goods imported from the U.S. as maybe a contributing factor to President Trump’s decision; however, it added that not all goods from the USA into Namibia attract customs duties as per the SACU tariff structure.

a6476.speaker: Falola Djogbénou Venise, president of WROP Benin (Platform of Beninese Organisations for Women’s Rights)
a6476.name: Falola Djogbénou Venise
a6476.title: president of WROP Benin (Platform of Beninese Organisations for Women’s Rights)
a6476.speech: Indicated that the results revolve around three advocacy priorities: social cohesion and peaceful coexistence; employability, empowerment and contribution to the local economy; and women’s political and administrative advancement, participation in governance and local development ; “I am delighted by the presentation of the results of this work, so that the next actions can be part of the drive to meet a major challenge: that of playing a decisive role in drafting and implementing important laws and policies relating to gender equity, and indeed equality, to women’s empowerment and to their representation in all decision-making bodies.”

a6476.speaker: Djamilatou Sabi Mohamed, president of the Caucus of Women Parliamentarians (Benin)
a6476.name: Djamilatou Sabi Mohamed
a6476.title: president of the Caucus of Women Parliamentarians (Benin)
a6476.speech: Set out the contribution of women parliamentarians at three levels: taking part in the community conversation sessions with 308 women leaders; the harmonisation workshop held in Parakou at which the community women’s advocacy plan and its implementation roadmap were drafted and validated; and the Caucus’s participation in the feedback workshop. On commitments made by women parliamentarians, she cited topical questions to the government, legislative initiatives, and the setting up of parliamentary information, resolution and inquiry commissions relating to women’s concerns on security issues.

a6476.speaker: Abigail Slenski, USAID representative
a6476.name: Abigail Slenski
a6476.title: USAID representative
a6476.speech: Explained that the OTI Regional Coastal Countries Support Programme (PRAPC) aims to strengthen social cohesion and support communities in limiting their vulnerability in the face of the current security situation ; “PRAPC works with the authorities at national and local level. It also works more closely with civil society organisations and youth and women’s associations, providing financial and technical support to their high-impact actions and initiatives in order to strengthen peace and social cohesion.”

a6476.speaker: Alain Orounla, Prefect of Littoral
a6476.name: Alain Orounla
a6476.title: Prefect of Littoral
a6476.speech: Declaring the proceedings open, advocated that the project be extended to the Littoral department and that men also be taken into account.

a6632.speaker: Antoine Kouton, Director General of SOBEMAP (Beninese Port Handling Company)
a6632.name: Antoine Kouton
a6632.title: Director General of SOBEMAP (Beninese Port Handling Company)
a6632.speech: Gave the minister a brief description of how the machinery used for loading and unloading containers operates and explained the difficulties his company faces: sometimes the equipment's parts break down in the middle of an operation, and their spare parts require strict observance of the rules prescribed by the Public Procurement Code, which prohibits direct-award contracts ; «If there are 2 or 3 ships berthing at the same time and they are handled at the same time, that is a plus for us.»

a6632.speaker: Samuel Batcho, Director General of the Autonomous Port of Cotonou (PAC)
a6632.name: Samuel Batcho
a6632.title: Director General of the Autonomous Port of Cotonou (PAC)
a6632.speech: «They have equipment but it does not work because they have parts that are damaged» ; explained to the minister that maintenance of the machinery, which is supposed to be provided by private contractors, is also subject to public procurement provisions; welcomed the minister's visit, which in his view aims at rallying the troops, and brought to his attention the glaring difficulties, particularly at SOBEMAP: «When a private handler's equipment breaks down, their spare parts are ordered immediately and it can operate again. But as far as SOBEMAP is concerned, you have to wait six months because of the provisions of the public procurement code. A whole procedure is required to buy the equipment's parts. The entire government should mobilise in order to remove certain locks as regards port activities.»

a6632.speaker: Patrick Yérima, Beninese Minister of the Maritime Economy and Port Infrastructure
a6632.name: Patrick Yérima
a6632.title: Beninese Minister of the Maritime Economy and Port Infrastructure
a6632.speech: «It is with satisfaction that I see first-hand what is being done here. My visit to SOBEMAP's installations, in particular its handling equipment, reveals some difficulties. I take good note of the directors general's requests, and between now and then they will be satisfied. Efforts will be made by the government to buy equipment for the company in order to make our Port more competitive. The government is implementing a number of reforms in order to make things easier for users of the port area.»

a6779.speaker: Alexandra Heldt, West Africa Regional Director of the Friedrich Naumann Foundation
a6779.name: Alexandra Heldt
a6779.title: West Africa Regional Director of the Friedrich Naumann Foundation
a6779.speech: Noted that "Africa possesses within itself the forces necessary to shape its own future. And in this process, the diaspora plays a strategic role." Said that every year billions are transferred to the continent, testifying to the diasporas' deep attachment to their land of origin, but that "the real challenge is now to transform this financial solidarity into productive investments capable of sustainably supporting innovation, infrastructure, education, health and entrepreneurship."

a6779.speaker: Alexandra Heldt, West Africa Regional Director of the Friedrich Naumann Foundation
a6779.name: Alexandra Heldt
a6779.title: West Africa Regional Director of the Friedrich Naumann Foundation
a6779.speech: "Diaspora bonds (bond issues floated by states) are not mere financial instruments; they symbolise a strong link between citizens and their nations, between the past and the future, between the desire to belong and the demand for development." Said they also embody a liberal approach founded on freedom, responsibility and voluntary commitment, allowing each person to contribute to the progress of their community not out of constraint but out of conviction, and stressed: "At the Friedrich Naumann Foundation, we firmly believe that lasting prosperity is born of economic freedom, creativity and civic responsibility, and diaspora bonds illustrate this vision: an African solution, carried by Africans, to build a common future."

a6779.speaker: Alexandra Heldt, West Africa Regional Director of the Friedrich Naumann Foundation
a6779.name: Alexandra Heldt
a6779.title: West Africa Regional Director of the Friedrich Naumann Foundation
a6779.speech: Argued that African countries should gain independence from foreign financing, observing: "The wars in Europe and the Middle East, just like the retreat of American aid, oblige us to rethink and optimise our resources, and to invest responsibly and sustainably."

a6779.speaker: Lanciné Diaby, Director General of Financing at Côte d'Ivoire's Ministry of Finance and Budget
a6779.name: Lanciné Diaby
a6779.title: Director General of Financing at Côte d'Ivoire's Ministry of Finance and Budget
a6779.speech: Noted that remittances from the African diaspora are precious resources for their countries of origin, and recalled that in 2024 remittances to Africa reached $92.2 billion, about 5.2% of the continent's GDP, and should exceed $100 billion in 2025.

a6779.speaker: World Bank
a6779.name: World Bank
a6779.speech: Cited as the source for the figure that the community of African emigrants today numbers no fewer than 140 million individuals worldwide.

a6779.speaker: Séraphin Prao, eminent Ivorian economist (professor)
a6779.name: Séraphin Prao
a6779.title: eminent Ivorian economist (professor)
a6779.speech: Indicated that since the pioneering experiences of Israel and India in the middle of the 20th century, many African countries such as Ethiopia, Nigeria and Senegal have successfully issued diaspora bonds; remarked that the state must inspire confidence in order to attract foreign currency through a diaspora bond, must have a long-term vision matched with innovative projects and above all must make strategic investments.

a6779.speaker: Stanislas Zézé, head of a financial rating agency
a6779.name: Stanislas Zézé
a6779.title: head of a financial rating agency
a6779.speech: Invited leaders to rethink the model for financing African economies, mentioning that with 54 countries whose currencies are non-convertible the mechanism will not be fully exploited; called for the question of currency convertibility to be settled and above all for the barriers to inter-state borrowing to be broken, while raising the possibility of opening diaspora bonds to other foreign countries according to the themes governing resource mobilisation.

a6853.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Malawi (statement)
a6853.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Malawi (statement)
a6853.speech: Says the plane carrying Chakwera is expected to touch down at Kamuzu International Airport at 15:45 hours.

a6853.speaker: President Lazarus Chakwera of Malawi
a6853.name: President Lazarus Chakwera of Malawi
a6853.speech: Delivered a statement during the UN General Assembly and general debate to mobilise global support for Malawi’s developmental priorities; during his address called for a collective approach in dealing with many challenges facing Malawi and other developing countries.

a6853.speaker: President Lazarus Chakwera of Malawi
a6853.name: President Lazarus Chakwera of Malawi
a6853.speech: In Washington DC, met the International Monetary Fund (IMF), World Bank and USAID heads at their respective headquarters where he appreciated their support to Malawi.

a6853.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank (AfDB)
a6853.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a6853.title: President of the African Development Bank (AfDB)
a6853.speech: Announced a grant of K95 billion to Malawi.

a6930.speaker: Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor, Majority Chief Whip of Ghana's Parliament
a6930.name: Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor
a6930.title: Majority Chief Whip of Ghana's Parliament
a6930.speech: Has accused the Ghana Bar Association (GBA) of politically sidelining President John Dramani Mahama in its upcoming annual conference, questioning the association's impartiality and commitment to fairness, and criticized that while former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo was almost always featured as a Special Guest of Honour and keynote speaker at GBA conferences between 2017 and 2024, the current President's name was conspicuously missing from the 2025 programme: "I have observed how the GBA organised its annual conference from 2017 to 2024. The then President, Nana Akufo-Addo, was nearly always the Special Guest of Honour and Speaker. That is not the case in 2025. The President is conspicuously missing from the list of advertised speakers at the confab" (on the social media platform X) ; "The GBA leadership has rather decided to invite the President of the Bar Council of England and Wales. GBA, kindly add the President of the Commonwealth Lawyers Association for effect" ; "What is curious is that the GBA leadership has instead chosen to invite the President of the Bar Council of England and Wales, a group that recently attacked this government without any provocation" ; "Your bias against John Mahama and the NDC government is too glaring to be ignored now. You can continue to act as a wing of the main opposition party to do its bidding we are ready for you."

a6930.speaker: Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor, Majority Chief Whip of Ghana's Parliament
a6930.name: Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor
a6930.title: Majority Chief Whip of Ghana's Parliament
a6930.speech: Stated, in a post shared on social media on Sunday, April 27, 2025, that the GBA resolution calling on President Mahama to revoke the suspension of Chief Justice Torkornoo, if indeed true, constitutes contempt of the Supreme Court's power, and pointed out that the action also amounts to an interference with the functions of the judiciary and a violation of the code of conduct for lawyers in Ghana: "Our very own Code of Conduct, the Legal Profession (Professional Conduct & Etiquette) Rules, 2020, LI 2423, forbids any lawyer or leaders of any lawyers' grouping from running any such unguarded commentaries or making such unprofessional public demands on a live case. Indeed, Regulation 89(c) of LI 2423, 2020 states as follows: 'a lawyer commits professional misconduct where the lawyer engages in a conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice'. The above provision forbids any member of the Bar or its leaders from upending the rights of one party in a case against the other part(ies). What the GBA leadership is engaged in is a front to the administration of justice and has the propensity to torpedo the independence of the judiciary they ostensibly seek to protect" ; He asserted that the resolution was politically motivated, urging President Mahama to ignore it: "This reported call by the GBA is very partisan & prejudicial as it affects a matter sub judice. The GBA leadership, like Caesar's wife, must live above reproach.
